in_greek.name: Τερέζα
in_greek.long_meaning: Όνομα που προέρχεται από την αραβική λέξη Teresa, που σημαίνει καλὴ γυνή, θερμός.  Στο χριστιανισμό, η Teresa είναι το όνομα της Αγίας Θηρεσίας του Ιησού, einer απο τις μεγαλύτερες θρησκευτικές θηριότρεσες της Ιστορίας.  Η Αγία Θηρεσία ήταν η πρώτη γυναίκα που έγινε καρδινάλης της Ρωμαιοκαθολικής Εκκλησίας.  Το όνομα Teresa χρησιμοποιείται επίσης για τις γυναίκες που έχουν μια θερμή και αληθινή θρησκευτική πίστη.

in_latin.name: Teresa
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen femininum, ab Arabico originem ducens, significans bona femina, fervens.  In Ecclesia Christi, Sancta Theresa, una ex maioribus religiosis feminis historiae, nomen habet.  Sancta Theresa prima femina erat qui Cardinalis Ecclesiae Catholicae Romanorum fieret.  Nomen Teresa etiam feminis, qui fide religiosa ferventi habent, datur.

in_english.name: Teresa
in_english.meaning: excellent woman, ardent, devout, chaste, of great worth
in_english.long_meaning: Name of a woman of great virtue and faith, originating from the Latin name 'Teresa', meaning excellent woman, ardent, devout, chaste, of great worth.  In Christian tradition, Saint Teresa of Jesus is a patron saint of those who have a deep love for God and a strong devotion to prayer and spiritual growth.  The name Teresa is also associated with women who are known for their kindness, generosity, and compassion.  In modern times, the name Teresa is popular among Christians and non-Christians alike, symbolizing the values of faith, hope, and charity.

saint_reference.note: Patron saint of those who have a deep love for God and a strong devotion to prayer and spiritual growth.

data.cultural_impact: Teresa has been a popular given name among Christians for centuries, with numerous prominent women bearing the name throughout history. Notable figures such as St. Teresa of Avila, St. Teresa of Calcutta (Mother Teresa), and Blessed Teresa of the Child Jesus were all named for their great works in spreading faith and kindness respectively. Additionally, Teresa is also a name in various cultures outside of Christianity, derived from Greek and Middle Eastern roots as well, highlighting its widespread appeal and significance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Teresa holds great spiritual significance for Christians, as it is often associated with the spiritual growth and transformation of the soul. This can be traced back to St. Teresa of Avila, a Spanish mystic and Carmelite nun, who was known for her writings on prayer and spirituality, and whose life inspired countless individuals to nurture their own faith. The name Teresa can be seen as a reminder of the joy and transformation that comes with a deep connection to one's faith and the divine, connecting the name to a legacy of spiritual growth and devotion.

historical_references.reference: Teresa of Avila (1515-1582) was a Spanish mystic and Carmelite nun who reformed the Carmelite Order and founded the Discalced Carmelites.
Teresa of Calcutta (1910-1997), also known as Mother Teresa, was an Albanian-Indian Roman Catholic nun and missionary.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Teresa remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Teresa from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Teresa - "Rejoice, Harvester". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Teresa: Derived from the Greek word "Teres," meaning reaper or harvester. In a spiritual context, Teresa represents the devoted soul who reaps the fruits of her labor in faith and love. Her name is also associated with St. Teresa of Avila, a renowned mystic and reformer, who cultivated her inner garden, bearing spiritual fruits for others.
